alt: Inside Lucas Oil Stadium with its retractable roof open, bright sunlight streaming through the gap and casting dramatic shadow stripes across the field while players warm up below
story: During the Colts' Week 3 win on September 27, 2026, Lucas Oil Stadium's retractable roof was opened for pleasant 72°F weather, instantly flooding the field with jarring half-light and half-shadow, prompting former Colts cornerback Darius Butler to post 'boy these shadows make for a TERRIBLE tv product' — the same complaint that has dogged the stadium since it opened in 2008.
why_funny: The entire engineering achievement of a retractable roof is to let you play in nice weather — but when the Colts open theirs, the sun hits at an angle that splits the field into a dramatic shadow/glare patchwork that makes the game unwatchable.
